detail.longDescription: How can I write a method in a typing.Protocol that is lenient to slight changes in function signature? For example, suppose I want to write a SupportsPut protocol that defines an abstract method named put . Both multiprocessing.Queue and queue.Queue of the standard library support the put operation of queues. However, they have an argument name mismatch ( obj vs item ): # in multiprocessing.Queue: def put(self, obj, block=True, timeout=None): ... # in queue.Queue: def put(self, item, block=True, timeout=None): ... So if I try to make them both SupportsPut s, I can only choose either obj or item as the abstract argument: class SupportsPut(Protocol): def put(self, item, block=True, timeout=None): ... def do_something_with(thing: SupportsPut): pass do_something_with(mp.Queue()) # <- do_something_with(q.Queue()) I get as expected a Pylance error that mp.Queue.put doesn’t conform to the protocol’s put . In theory, do_something_with could just treat obj and item positionally, by calling put(object) instead of put(obj=object) / put(item=object) , making both queue implementations valid SupportsPut s. But I don’t know how to let the protocol method know that. This is just an example of the “slight difference in function signature” I mentioned. Maybe one implementation offers more kwargs than the other; maybe one has / or * specifiers; maybe one has an argument with a narrower type; etc. In most of these cases the difference can be worked around by the user function do_something_with by calling the methods in a specific way as shown above. But does Protocol allow this kind of flexibility? Should it? How should my example above be done?
